action.title: Root analysis

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc B580, HLSL cs_6_10, raw ByteAddressBuffer/RWByteAddressBuffer, WaveSize(32) preferred; SM 6.10 thread-scope FP16 linalg supports useful 16x32/16x64-like matvec fragments.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Real MatrixScope::Thread FP16 linalg fragments run correctly on the target and map well to the dense C=32/hidden=128 reductions.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Fused design eliminates global phase tensors and only reads input/state and writes final output.

register_pressure.notes: Current best keeps many arrays per live token, especially q/k/v, attention, context, residuals, and 128 MLP activations.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: does: The best evaluated subtree now has a fully fused single-dispatch HLSL SM 6.10 linalg shader for the fixed 4x4-window transformer block. bottleneck: likely compute and register pressure more than memory bandwidth, because the shader avoids intermediate global writes but holds many per-token arrays and uses dense matvec plus exp/tanh math.
FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent: yes for the active child; root remains only a dummy grouping node.
UPDATE_BELIEF: The linalg wave-owned mapping is no longer speculative: it passed at 3.981224 ms, 28.861x faster than the CPU reference. next bet: refine the successful family by improving lane utilization and register pressure before pursuing more disruptive scalar/shared-memory alternatives.

action.description: Implement a maximally fused single-dispatch shader where one WaveSize(32) wave owns one 4x4 window, lanes 0..15 own tokens, dense Linear fragments use real SM 6.10 FP16 MatrixScope::Thread matvec calls where K=32 fits, and attention exchange uses wave intrinsics with register-resident intermediates.
action.rationale: This directly matches the fixed N=16,C=32 structure, avoids global intermediate round-trips, avoids group barriers, and gives early high-value evidence for the required linalg path. M=16,K=32 linalg fragments naturally cover qkv/proj/fc1/fc2 output-channel blocks, with Multiply<float16_t> widened into FP32 glue where needed.
action.title: Wave-owned full-window fused block with SM 6.10 linalg projections

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Uses [WaveSize(32)] and thread-scope Matrix<ComponentType::F16,16,32,MatrixUse::A,MatrixScope::Thread> style fragments; bracket indexing required for vector widths above 4.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The evaluated linalg path is a good hardware fit for Arc B580 and remains the dominant successful family.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Wave-owned fused execution avoids intermediate tensor writes and keeps traffic largely to model reads plus final stores.

register_pressure.notes: The family is fast but live state per active lane is large; child evidence suggests further gains require register/live-range reduction.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT:
- does: Top-level end-to-end family where a wave owns a complete 4x4 Swin window and uses SM 6.10 thread-scope linalg for dense projections. It relies on wave intrinsics for token exchange rather than groupshared memory.
- bottleneck: compute/register pressure, not synchronization; the wave-local design avoids group barriers.
FOLLOW_THROUGH:
- aligned_with_intent: yes
- if_no: N/A
UPDATE_BELIEF:

action.description: Implement a fused shader where a threadgroup processes several independent windows and cooperatively stages selected high-reuse model state as a compact read-only groupshared tile, then each wave computes one window mostly with scalar FP16/FP32 loops.
action.rationale: The model state is small and reused for every window. Loading selected weights once per group can reduce logical state traffic versus per-wave SRV streaming, while still preserving full operation fusion and avoiding global intermediates.
action.title: Multi-window shared-state scalar/cache family

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Avoids dependence on linalg PSO support; uses scalar/vector HLSL under cs_6_10 raw-buffer constraints. Multiple waves per group each own independent windows.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Dense projections and MLP are scalar wave-lane dot products rather than the measured SM 6.10 linalg path. The result is compute-limited and substantially slower than the linalg two-window family despite lower model-state traffic.

memory_bandwidth.notes: All model tensors are cooperatively staged as read-only reusable groupshared tiles. Producer set is the full 1024-thread group; consumers are all 32 waves/windows after one GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync. Reuse is up to 32 windows per group, but the 25.9 KiB tile load plus lower occupancy reduces the realized bandwidth benefit.

register_pressure.notes: Each wave keeps q/k/v for 16 tokens plus logits and MLP temporaries in registers. The scalar fused path avoids global intermediates but carries many live values through attention and MLP loops.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT:
- does: The evaluated shader launches 32 waves/1024 threads per group; each wave owns one 4x4 window and computes LayerNorm, QKV, attention, projection, residual, second LayerNorm, and MLP fully fused. It stages RPE, norms, biases, QKV/proj/fc weights as read-only reusable groupshared tiles produced cooperatively by the full group and consumed by all waves after a single barrier, with nominal reuse across 32 independent windows.
- bottleneck: compute and occupancy/register pressure dominate; bandwidth savings from groupshared state caching did not compensate for scalar dense loops, large threadgroups, and the one large cooperative preload.
FOLLOW_THROUGH:
- aligned_with_intent: yes
UPDATE_BELIEF:
- what changed after eval_result? This family is correct but much weaker than the wave-owned linalg path: 14.256 ms / 8.11x versus the current best around 3.98 ms / 28.7x. The evidence suggests model-state caching alone is not the key lever for this fixed small-C Swin block.
- next bet: If continuing this branch, try a smaller group and a trimmed shared cache that only keeps the highest-reuse compact tables/biases, while streaming dense weights from SRV/L2 or moving dense work to linalg. Otherwise prioritize refinements under the proven dual-halfwave linalg branch.
PERF_GAP:
- expected_vs_observed: predicted latency factor was about 0.045 of reference; observed was about 0.1233 of reference.
- hypothesized_reason: expected model-weight traffic reduction was outweighed by scalar compute throughput, 1024-thread-group scheduling/occupancy costs, and large live register working sets.

action.description: Implement a fused shader where an entire threadgroup owns one 4x4 window with channel-parallel work for LayerNorm, projections, attention, and MLP, using groupshared exchange/reduction scratch for q/k/v and token reductions.
action.rationale: This reduces per-thread register burden and gives a robust fallback if one-lane-per-token full fusion spills. It exposes more threads per window for C=32 and hidden=128 reductions, at the cost of explicit shared exchange and synchronization.
action.title: Threadgroup-owned window with cooperative channel partitioning

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Works within cs_6_10 without relying on threadgroup linalg. Must keep groupshared below 32 KiB and minimize GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync calls.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Cooperative channel partitioning is less naturally matched to proven Thread-scope linalg matvec fragments and may lose the high-throughput dense path used by the best evaluated branch.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Could reuse some input/state data cooperatively, but likely needs groupshared exchange or extra global traffic for per-token/channel handoff. It risks spending bandwidth on materialization that the wave-owned design avoids.

register_pressure.notes: May reduce per-thread live set by splitting channels, but the reduction comes with cross-thread accumulation and synchronization complexity.

action.title: Two half-active WaveSize(32) waves per threadgroup for two 4x4 windows

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Measured best solution confirms Arc B580 handles the Thread-scope FP16 linalg fragments well for this fixed Swin-block shape. The ownership plan remains the best evaluated top-level path.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Best measured branch uses raw FP16 loads and avoids extra global intermediate tensors. No groupshared cache is needed because wave-local exchange via WaveReadLaneAt handles attention data reuse.

register_pressure.notes: The design is fast but close to a register-pressure limit because each active lane owns one token and a full channel/MLP working set. Child micro-refinement that did not reduce live ranges regressed slightly.

action.title: Micro-refine best dual-halfwave linalg shader around conversion and residual glue

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Real SM 6.10 MatrixScope::Thread linalg fragments are used for QKV/proj/MLP dense multiplies and match the proven Arc B580 path. Bottleneck appears to be compute/register latency rather than synchronization.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Raw-buffer FP16 inputs/state keep traffic compact and no groupshared staging is used. Remaining bandwidth pressure is mostly repeated per-lane state/bias/gamma loads and full input feature reads per token.

register_pressure.notes: Wave-owned token mapping keeps all intermediates in registers, but q/k/v, attention row, context, MLP activations, and linalg vectors create a large live set. The micro-refinement did not reduce this enough and may have slightly worsened occupancy/spills.

It uses SM 6.10 MatrixScope::Thread FP16 linalg for QKV, projection, and MLP dense fragments, keeps attention/residual/layernorm glue in registers, and writes packed FP16 output.
- bottleneck: compute/register-latency dominated, with secondary register pressure and repeated state loads; sync is essentially absent and bandwidth is not the primary limiter.

kernel_summary: This is a single-dispatch fp16 fused Swin-window block for fixed input (1,720,1280,32) with 57,600 independent 4x4 windows, single-head N=16 attention, two LayerNorms over C=32, dense Linear reductions 32->96, 32->32, 32->128, 128->32, GELU, residuals, and final fp16 output. The best initial hypothesis is full fusion with one wave owning one window: keep per-token/intermediate values in registers, exchange q/k/v via wave intrinsics, use stable FP32 reductions for LN/softmax glue, and honestly prototype SM 6.10 FP16 thread-scope linalg for dense matvec fragments. Main risks are linalg PSO/codegen, numerical equivalence of FP16/FP32 accumulation versus PyTorch, register spills from full fusion, and whether tiny model weights are sufficiently cache-resident or need selective groupshared read-only tiling under the 32 KiB limit.
open_questions: Does the local Intel Arc B580 driver accept the intended cs_6_10 MatrixScope::Thread M=16,K=32 FP16 linalg fragments inside a large fused shader with raw ByteAddressBuffer bindings?
Is Multiply<float16_t> with FP32 glue accumulation numerically close enough to PyTorch/XPU fp16 Linear and attention results under rtol=0.01, atol=0.01, especially for qkv/proj/fc2?
What is the practical register count and spill behavior for one-wave-per-window full fusion when q/k/v, softmax row, residual, LN2, fc1 GELU, and fc2 accumulators are kept live or streamed?
Are model weights reliably retained in cache across 57,600 windows, or does explicit groupshared read-only state tiling materially improve GPU timestamp despite the preload barrier and 32 KiB cap?
Which GELU formula is used by the evaluator's PyTorch path for fp16 on XPU, and is the tanh approximation acceptable within tolerance or must erf-based GELU be used?
What launch geometry gives best occupancy for the runner on Arc B580 when the dispatch counts are fixed in launch.json and no root constants or temporary buffers are available?
Can raw UAV fp16 output packing with 4-byte alignment safely write pairs of half values without touching padded or invalid tensor bytes at the end of the buffer?
